subject: general
question: Heavy water is so called because:

options.text: it uses Deuterium, a heavier isotope of hydrogen, rather than Protium.
its density is three times that of normal water.
it is used in nuclear reactors.
it is used by the heavy industries such as steel, chemicals etc.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Heavy water is known as such because it uses **Deuterium**, a heavier isotope of hydrogen, rather than Protium.
 
• Deuterium has one proton and one neutron, making it heavier than Protium, which has only one proton and no neutrons.
 
• Heavy water (D₂O) is used in certain types of nuclear reactors as a neutron moderator.
 
• Its density is slightly higher than that of normal water (H₂O), but it is not three times denser.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Deuterium is a stable isotope of hydrogen with a natural abundance in Earth's oceans of about one atom in 6420 of hydrogen.
 
• Heavy water was first produced in 1932, and it has since been used in various scientific and industrial applications.
 
• The presence of deuterium in heavy water gives it different nuclear properties, which are crucial for its role in nuclear reactors.
